descripcion: Nada brewery with five centuries of history, the oldest documented sake label in Japan. Keeps the fune press and has not changed its label since 1505.
Brewery in the Nada district of Kobe, with its own museum in a wooden kura rebuilt after the 1995 earthquake. Shop on its own domain.
Maker of Fukuju, the sake served at the Nobel banquet since 2008. Its grounds bring together kura, restaurant and concert hall.
Brewery founded in 1662 in the Nishinomiya-go district, with its own sake museum and bulk sales at its Hakushika Classics shop.
Brewery founded in 1743 in Nada and the largest sake producer in Japan. Keeps its wooden kura as a museum open to the public.
Nishinomiya-go brewery and sole supplier of ritual sake to the Ise shrine since 1924. Works with the area's miyamizu water.
Brewery founded in 1659 in Nada, a reference for the dry kimoto style. Its site returned 403 at review time.
Nada brewery that gave rise to kyokai yeast number one and to the use of Masamune itself as a sake name. Its domain did not respond.
